He shall come, &c.--</hi>This answer was given by the Pharisees themselves (<reference osisRef="Matt.21.41">Mt 21:41</reference>), thus pronouncing their own righteous doom. entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14716"/><div sID="gen28434" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14716"/><hi type="bold">17-19. written--</hi>(in <reference osisRef="Ps.118.22">Psa 118:22</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ps.118.23">23</reference>. See on <reference osisRef="Luke.19.38">Lu 19:38</reference>). The Kingdom of God is here a Temple, in the erection of which a certain stone, rejected as unsuitable by the spiritual builders, is, by the great Lord of the House, made the keystone of the whole. On that Stone the builders were now "falling" and being "broken" (<reference osisRef="Isa.8.15">Is 8:15</reference>), "sustaining great spiritual hurt; but soon that Stone should fall upon them and grind them to powder" (<reference osisRef="Dan.2.34">Da 2:34</reference>, 35; <reference osisRef="Zech.12.3">Zec 12:3</reference>)--in their corporate capacity in the tremendous destruction of Jerusalem, but personally, as unbelievers, in a more awful sense still. <div eID="gen28434" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 17-19. written-- (in Psa 118:22 , 23 . See on Lu 19:38 ). entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14724"/><div sID="gen28444" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14724"/><hi type="bold">36. neither ... die any more--</hi>Marriage is ordained to perpetuate the human family; but as there will be no breaches by death in the future state, this ordinance will cease.<div eID="gen28444" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28445" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">equal--</hi>or "like."<div eID="gen28445" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28446" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">unto the angels--</hi>that is, in the immortality of their nature.<div eID="gen28446" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen28447" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">children of God--</hi>not in respect of character but nature; "being the children of the resurrection" to an undecaying existence (<reference osisRef="Rom.8.21">Ro 8:21</reference>, <reference osisRef="Rom.8.23">23</reference>). And thus the children of their Father's immortality (<reference osisRef="1Tim.6.16">1Ti 6:16</reference>). <div eID="gen28447" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 36. neither ... die any more-- Marriage is ordained to perpetuate the human family; but as there will be no breaches by death in the future state, this ordinance will cease. equal-- or "like." unto the angels-- that is, in the immortality of their nature. children of God-- not in respect of character but nature; "being the children of the resurrection" to an undecaying existence ( Ro 8:21 , 23 ). And thus the children of their Father's immortality ( 1Ti 6:16 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv14728"/><title type="x-s3"><reference osisRef="Luke.20.41-Luke.20.47">Lu 20:41-47</reference>. Christ Baffles the Pharisees by a Question about David and Messiah, and Denounces the Scribes.</title> <div sID="gen28452" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv14728"/><hi type="bold">41. said, &c.--</hi>"What think ye of Christ [the promised and expected Messiah]? Whose son is He [to be]? They say unto Him, The son of David. He saith unto them, How then doth David in spirit [by the Holy Ghost, Mr 12:36] call Him Lord?" (<reference osisRef="Matt.22.42">Mt 22:42</reference>, <reference osisRef="Matt.22.43">43</reference>). The difficulty can only be solved by the higher and lower--the divine and human natures of our Lord (<reference osisRef="Matt.1.23">Mt 1:23</reference>). Mark the testimony here given to the inspiration of the Old Testament (compare <reference osisRef="Luke.24.44">Lu 24:44</reference>). <div eID="gen28452" type="x-p"/>
